newsitem.title: FRANCE: New French anti-racism bill may come up in January.
newsitem.headline: New French anti-racism bill may come up in January.

text.p: A new draft bill to toughen French anti-racism laws may come up for a vote in the National Assembly in January or February, according to a preliminary schedule of parliamentary events released on Tuesday.

The bill, proposed by Justice Minister Jacques Toubon after new controversy caused by anti-immigrant politician Jean-Marie Le Pen, would make anyone making a racist statement in public liable to a year in prison and a 300,000 franc ($60,000) fine.
Sanctions would increase to two years in jail and a 500,000 franc ($100,000) fine if the remark were judged an incitement to discrimination, hatred or violence.
Critics in government ranks and the opposition have however warned that the bill was so sweeping that it threatened basic freedoms such as freedom of speech.
Toubon unveiled plans to stiffen legislation after Le Pen, whose National Front party proposes sending immigrants home, said last month racial inequality was "a fact".
Toubon, a conservative, then said the remark was too vague for him to be prosecuted under existing laws and a new bill was needed.

The bill widens the scope of existing legislation to include statements aimed at "an ethnic group, a nation, a race or a religion" and extends the statute of limitations to one year from three months.

Le Pen, who has in the past dismissed the Nazi gas chambers as a mere detail in the history of World War Two, won 15 percent of the vote in 1995 presidential elections. Prime Minister Alain Juppe last month branded him "deeply, almost viscerally racist, anti-Semitic and xenophobic".
